m.chalisa.do1: Bowing my head with love at the lotus feet of Śrī Gaṇapati and of the Guru, I tell the Chālīsā of the nine planets; Sarasvatī is my helper.
m.chalisa.do2: Victory, victory to the Sun, to Śaśi and Soma, the Moon, and to Budha; victory to Guru Bṛhaspati, to Śukra of Bhṛgu's line and to King Śani. Victory to the planets Rāhu and Ketu: be gracious today.
m.chalisa.cau1: First of all I bow my head to the Sun: knowing this servant to be helpless, be gracious.
m.chalisa.cau2: O Āditya, Divākara, Bhānu: I am dull of mind and deeply ignorant.
m.chalisa.cau3: Now take away the afflictions of your own servant, O maker of the day, lord of the day in twelve forms.
m.chalisa.cau4: Salutations to you, Bhāskara, Sūrya, Prabhākara, Arka, Mitra; you make sin vain and you forgive.
m.chalisa.cau5: O Śaśi, Mayaṅka, lord of the night, Master, Candra, treasury of the digits: salutations; I bow to you.
m.chalisa.cau6: O lord of the full-moon night, cool-rayed Himāṃśu, Rākeśa: take away the afflictions of the body of the devotee who bows to you.
m.chalisa.cau7: You are Soma, Indu and Vidhu, the peaceful Sudhākara, the cool-rayed, lord of the healing herbs, and Niśākara, maker of the night.
m.chalisa.cau8: It is you who shine on the beautiful forehead of Śiva. I take refuge in you, I take refuge: take away the afflictions of your servant.
m.chalisa.cau9: Victory, victory, victory to Maṅgala (Mars), giver of happiness, famed by the names Lohita, the red one, Bhauma, son of the Earth, and others.
m.chalisa.cau10: O Aṅgāraka, O Kuja, remover of disease and debt: have mercy; this is our prayer.
m.chalisa.cau11: O Mahīsuta, O Kṣitisuta, son of the Earth, store of happiness, red-limbed one: victory to you, destroyer of your devotees' sins.
m.chalisa.cau12: Now take away misfortune past fathoming, and fulfil every wish.
m.chalisa.cau13: Victory to you, great King Budha (Mercury), son of the Moon: do good works for all people.
m.chalisa.cau14: Grant strength of intellect and good sense, wise one; take away hard troubles and bring about our good.
m.chalisa.cau15: O son of Tārā, son of Rohiṇī, son of the Moon, destroyer of sorrow and strife.
m.chalisa.cau16: Fulfil your servant's hope, Master. Lord, protector of those who bow to you: salutations; I bow to you.
m.chalisa.cau17: Victory, victory, victory to Śrī Gurudeva (Jupiter). Lord, may I always serve you.
m.chalisa.cau18: You are the teacher of the gods, the gods' Guru and the wise one; you are Indra's priest and the giver of learning.
m.chalisa.cau19: You are Vācaspati and Vāgīśa, lord of speech, and generous; Jīva and Bṛhaspati are your names.
m.chalisa.cau20: You are an ocean of learning, and Aṅgirā is your name: fulfil every wish in every way.
m.chalisa.cau21: This servant meditates without ceasing on the lotus soles of Śukradeva (Venus).
m.chalisa.cau22: O Uśanā, Bhārgava, son of Bhṛgu, priest of the Daityas, destroyer of the wicked.
m.chalisa.cau23: Ornament of Bhṛgu's line, remover of faults: take away the harmful planets and make us happy.
m.chalisa.cau24: You are the best of Brahmins and the crown of astrologers; you alone are king of the human body.
m.chalisa.cau25: Victory to Śrī Śanideva (Saturn), son of the Sun; victory to the dark one, Sauri, whom the world reveres.
m.chalisa.cau26: Piṅgala, Manda, Raudra and Yama are your names, and Vapra and others, and Koṇastha the excellent.
m.chalisa.cau27: Your gaze is sidelong, and your form graces the pipal tree; in a moment you make a man a pauper, in a moment a king.
m.chalisa.cau28: With your lovely golden feet you make men blessed; take away calamity, O son of Chāyā.
m.chalisa.cau29: Victory, victory to Rāhu, who enters the sky; it is you who seize the Moon and the Sun.
m.chalisa.cau30: Foe of the Sun and the Moon, you have taken the name Svarbhānu; Śikhī and many others are your names.
m.chalisa.cau31: You are Saiṃhikeya, son of Siṃhikā, king of the demons. Half-bodied one, keep the world's honour.
m.chalisa.cau32: If, as a planet, you find your time and come anywhere, always bring forth peace and happiness.
m.chalisa.cau33: Victory to Śrī Ketu, remover of hard sorrows; bringer of good, work the welfare of good people.
m.chalisa.cau34: You bear a banner; your form is a headless trunk, and dreadful; you are fearsome, terrible of body, the crusher of sin, and dark.
m.chalisa.cau35: You are Śikhī, the crested star, and a mighty planet; great is your majesty, and your splendour knows no bound.
m.chalisa.cau36: Your mount is a fish, and you bring great good. Holding mercy in your heart, grant peace.
m.chalisa.cau37: Near Prayāga, king of places of pilgrimage, lives Sundaradāsa, servant of Śrī Rāma,
m.chalisa.cau38: in the village of Kakarā, at Pure-Tivārī, by Durvāsā's hermitage, which takes away people's sorrows.
m.chalisa.cau39: He wrote this prayer for the peace of the nine planets for the sake of happiness; it is a bridge to carry people across the troubles of the body.
m.chalisa.cau40: Whoever recites it daily with his mind intent on it enjoys every happiness and attains the supreme state.
m.chalisa.do3: Blessed are the nine planet gods, the Lords; their glory is unfathomable and boundless. They fill the mind and the home with new blessings and joy, and are the door to happiness for the people of the world.
m.chalisa.do4: This Chālīsā of the nine planets was composed by Sundaradāsa. When it is read with love, happiness grows, and every joy and delight.
